provenance.text: Single-author project. Two layers: (1) knowledge base `entries/` = 518 JSON concept entries (519 files under entries/ in the tree) - authorship method (human vs LLM) is NOT stated; (2) `train.jsonl` (= identical-size copy `software-strategist-v1.jsonl`) = 13,491 synthetic chat examples generated by an LLM "teacher" from the entries via tools/generate_synthetic.py. The card does NOT name the model used. The script supports an OpenAI-compatible endpoint (example "Qwen"), OpenAI Codex CLI (gpt-5.5) and Claude Code CLI (claude-opus-4-7) with fallback chains.

quotes.quote: A language-agnostic knowledge base of software engineering fundamentals, paired with a synthetic instruction-tuning dataset (~13,500 examples) for training small language models (SLMs) as **software engineering strategists**.

The training data is synthesized from a curated knowledge base of 518 language-agnostic software engineering concepts, each encoding the strategic reasoning behind when to apply a concept, when to avoid it, and what anti-patterns to watch for.
The dataset is composed of approximately **60% single-concept**, **25% multi-concept**, and **15% null** examples.

**`generate_synthetic.py`** — Generates synthetic training examples from the knowledge base, supporting multiple backends and fallback chains ... These tools are provided so users can regenerate or expand the dataset with their own LLM backends.

Supports multiple backends with automatic fallback:
  - openai: Any OpenAI-compatible API endpoint
  - codex: OpenAI Codex CLI (gpt-5.5)
  - claude: Claude Code CLI (claude-opus-4-7)
...
    # Multi-backend with fallback (try Qwen first, fall back to Codex/Claude on failure)

You are generating synthetic training data for a software engineering strategy model. ... Generate <<N>> training examples based on the concept below. ... The user message must NEVER mention the concept name, category, or ID.
All 518 entries score a perfect **14/14** on this rubric.  [self-reported; rubric pass threshold ">=1 per dimension and >=7/14 total"]

upstream_sources.detail: No external dataset/corpus cited as a source. contamination_notes: Card says nothing about benchmarks. No SWE-bench/BFCL/ToolACE/HumanEval derivation is claimed or visible; LANDSCAPE.md mentions BigCodeBench only as a comparison point. Content is concept-level advice with no repo code. Low apparent contamination risk; not formally verifiable.

schema.name: messages
schema.meaning: 3 messages: system (one of several randomized strategist prompts from tools/system_prompts.json), user (situation description, never naming the concept), assistant (a JSON STRING).

schema.name: messages[2].content -> concepts_applied
schema.meaning: 0-3 routed concepts, id like "sf-error-classification-001", weight e.g. "primary". Empty list for "null" examples.

schema.name: messages[2].content -> core_idea
schema.meaning: 2-3 sentence strategic framing for the situation; null for null examples.

schema.name: messages[2].content -> key_principles
schema.meaning: 3-5 actionable principles (closest thing to "when/how to use").

schema.name: messages[2].content -> avoid
schema.meaning: 1-3 warnings = the anti-pattern / "what not to do" signal in the TRAINING rows.

schema.name: entries/sf-*.json (knowledge base, NOT in the train split)
schema.meaning: id, concept, category, subcategory, difficulty, core_idea, when_to_use (2-5 strings), when_not_to_use (2-5 strings), anti_patterns [{name, description, why_bad}] (1-3), reasoning_chain [{step, question, insight, principle}] (3-6; tradeoff analysis lives here), examples [{language, scenario, code, explanation}], related_concepts [{concept, relationship, id}], tags, task_types.

example_row_summary: row 0: system="You help developers understand the strategic engineering concepts behind their problems. Respond with JSON: concepts_applied (0-3 with id/name/weight), core_idea, key_principles, avoid."; user="How do I declare a constant in Swift?"; assistant='{"concepts_applied": [], "core_idea": null, "key_principles": [], "avoid": []}' (a NULL example).
row 1: user="What is the curl command to send a POST request with a JSON body to http://example.com/api?"; assistant = same empty JSON.

All first 100 rows served by /first-rows are NULL examples (concepts_applied == []), i.e. the file is ordered with the ~15% null block first. Non-null rows were not inspected (card example: concepts_applied=[{"id":"sf-error-classification-001","name":"Error Classification","weight":"primary"}], core_idea="Classify errors as transient (retryable) vs permanent (fail-fast)...").

IMPORTANT for the decision corpus: explicit when_to_use / when_not_to_use / anti_patterns(why_bad) / reasoning_chain fields exist ONLY in the 518 entries/ files, not in the 13,491 training rows (which only carry key_principles + avoid). There is no dedicated "tradeoffs" field anywhere; tradeoffs are inside reasoning_chain/when_not_to_use per SCHEMA.md.
surprises: Claims check: ~13.5k examples -> 13,491 CONFIRMED; 518 concepts -> card says 518, tree lists 519 files under entries/.
License claim was unspecified by the lead; actual = MIT (card + LICENSE file, Copyright (c) 2026 Jeremy Tregunna). Citation bibtex says year 2025, CITATION.cff says release-date 2026-05-15.

Generating model is not disclosed; script defaults include proprietary-provider models (OpenAI gpt-5.5 via Codex CLI, Anthropic claude-opus-4-7 via Claude Code CLI) as fallbacks. If any rows came from those, provider terms on using outputs to train competing models could be relevant - cannot be determined from the repo.

Repo ships internal agent config and session logs (.pi/agent-sessions/*.json, ~620 KB) even though .gitignore lists ".pi/"; also a compiled tools/__pycache__/*.pyc and a byte-identical-size duplicate of the training file (software-strategist-v1.jsonl and train.jsonl both 21,376,462 bytes).
Very new, single-author, low-usage dataset (created 2026-05-16, 123 downloads); quality claim "14/14 on rubric" is self-assessed.
Card "Schema" lists 19 categories; SCHEMA.md is "v0.1"/"taxonomy v0.2".
